ety.text: From coma (“hair”). Can be analyzed as the perfect passive participle of a first-conjugation verb *comō (“to be furnished with hair”), but only this perfect participle form and the present active participle form comāns are attested in Classical Latin, and post-classical uses of other verb forms are rare.
